summary: Code-review platforms can enforce that findings are resolved, dismissed by an authorized reviewer, or blocked before merge. They provide the state machine for a council loop; the quality of findings and acceptance rationales still requires project policy.

items.text: GitHub protected branches can require pull-request reviews, successful status checks, and resolution of every review conversation before merge; stale approvals can be dismissed when the reviewed diff changes.

GitLab merge requests combine assigned reviewers, approval rules, discussions, CI results, and merge checks in one record; unresolved feedback can remain a visible blocker instead of disappearing into an agent transcript.
Gerrit submit requirements express project-specific, query-based conditions for when a change is submittable and display satisfied, unsatisfied, and overridden states with applicability rules.
GitLab approval rules can require specified numbers and groups of approvers and control whether authors or committers may self-approve, supporting explicit authority for accepting a council finding.
